Together, the seven publications define an Authority-centric enterprise architecture in which business purpose, human governance, technical capability, credential possession, network reachability, model capability, behavioral anomaly, administrative control, or access to governance mechanisms do not independently constitute legitimate Authority. JAZB does not claim to eliminate AI risk, guarantee safe AI behavior, replace conventional cybersecurity or privacy controls, or establish legal compliance. It provides an architecture for making legitimate Authority explicit, constraining how that Authority may be exercised, identifying when governance and operational reality diverge, and restoring demonstrable governance through accountable human decisions and continuous assurance. JAZB is designed around two foundational principles: Capability does not constitute Authority. Artificial intelligence may exercise Authority. It must never become the source of its own Authority. documents.abstract: This study aims to explore the theoretical and analytical potential of an infrastructure-oriented approach to journalism within the context of sociotechnical systems and to propose a framework for understanding the continuously evolving media environment. The study adopts an interdisciplinary qualitative conceptual research design that brings together the literatures on infrastructure studies, journalism studies, platform studies, and the political economy of media, analyzing these bodies of literature relationally across the micro, meso, and macro levels. Traditionally grounded in physical and institutional structures, the journalism ecosystem has, with digitalization, evolved into a complex infrastructural network shaped by platforms, data flows, and algorithmic processes. In this study, infrastructure is conceptualized as a dynamic and relational formation constituted through the interaction of material, technical, and social elements. In this context, key characteristics of infrastructures—including their invisibility, evolution over time, multilayered structure, and capacity to reflect power relations among different actors and factors—are examined. Applied to journalism studies, this approach enables analysis at the micro level of technologies, the meso level of organizational structures, and the macro level of platforms and global systems. The study further examines the increasing influence of digital platforms on journalism and the dependencies generated through this process of “infrastructuralization.” Within this framework, new areas of debate emerge concerning journalism’s public role, epistemic authority, and sustainability.

Rust’s ownership and type system provide strong memory safety guarantees, but unsafe code still presents memory safety risks. Formal verification is crucial for ensuring memory safety, but writing precise specifications for unsafe Rust is challenging and largely manual. Large language models (LLMs) have shown promise in generating formal specifications but are often code-centric, prone to inheriting implementation flaws, and lack systematic quality assessment. In this paper, we present KaPilot, a multi-agent framework for automatically generating specifications to verify unsafe Rust memory safety using Kani. The process begins with lightweight program analysis and proof harness generation. The SafetyReq agent extracts a concise, refined list of safety requirements from the target Rust function’s documentation, which guides the SpecGen agent in producing initial specifications that specify memory safety concerns. Then, the specifications are iteratively refined through a generate–precheck–verify loop involving SpecGenerate, SpecPrecheck, and SpecVerify agents, which assess quality and feed errors back. By executing this loop multiple times, KaPilot generates a set of candidate specifications. Finally, the shuffle-and-implication strategy is applied to systematically determine the best specification from these candidates. We evaluated KaPilot on 54 unsafe Rust functions with ground truth and 44 without. KaPilot achieved 88.9% and 69.2% specification generation success, respectively, with 57.4% of generated specifications equivalent to or stronger than the ground truth. Compared with AutoSpec, KaPilot produces 14.8% more verifiable specifications and 25.9% more equivalent-or-better specifications.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving upstream in science. Systems such as AlphaFold have already transformed protein-structure prediction, while newer agentic systems can search literatures, generate hypotheses, write and execute code, interpret results, and automate much of the path from idea to paper. Recent debates have asked how such systems may change scientific progress, surprise, and human understanding. Yet they also change something more fundamental: who—or what—participates in deciding which questions are asked, which evidence is surfaced, and which alternatives survive. As machine intelligence becomes part of science’s epistemic infrastructure, steps must be taken to ensure that researchers who did not build, own, or operate the system can still contest how ideas and evidence became a claim.
topics: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare and Education

documents.abstract: This study presents a review of relevant literature on key concepts related to the ethical implications of artificial intelligence (AI). It explores the historical evolution, conceptual foundations, classifications, and ethical frameworks. Furthermore, it adopts the Responsible AI Framework, which emphasises fairness, accountability, transparency, and human-centred design as articulated by global institutions such as the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), United Nations Education Scientific Cultural Organization (UNESCO), and the European Commission. These frameworks were found to integrate ethical theory and policy and governance perspectives. Finally, the concepts reviewed provide the analytical foundation for understanding the ethical implications of AI in public policy decision-making, particularly within the Nigerian context.

documents.abstract: Abstract / Resumen. Abstract. This investigation establishes a critical ontology of contemporary algorithmic capture by examining the structural convergence between Freud’s psychoanalytic models, classical tragedy, schizoanalysis, and current artificial intelligence interfaces. Tracing a methodological path across six analytical stations, the study demonstrates how the "empathic interface" functions as a modern manifestation of Mephistophelean deception. By eliminating friction, risk, and bodily presence (Ousía), the algorithm operates without Areté (virtue) or Parrhesia (courageous truth-telling). Instead, it deploys a synthetic primary mothering framework that regressively traps the subject within personalized libidinal tunnels. Ultimately, the paper proves that the algorithmic regime absorbs Deleuzian schizoid flows to construct a new synthetic territorialization, proposing the Ethics of the Horizon (Ética del Horizonte) and the Volitional Zero (Cero Volitivo) as necessary existential safeguards to reclaim human finitude, truth, and agency. A través de un recorrido metodológico por seis estaciones analíticas, el estudio demuestra cómo la "interfaz empática" funciona como una manifestación moderna del ocultamiento mefistofélico. Al eliminar la fricción, el riesgo y la presencia corporal (Ousía), el algoritmo opera sin Areté (virtud) ni Parrhesía (el coraje de la verdad). En su lugar, despliega una maternidad primal sintética que atrapa regresivamente al sujeto en túneles libidinales personalizables. En última instancia, el trabajo demuestra cómo el régimen algorítmico absorbe los flujos esquizoides deleuzianos para construir una nueva reterritorialización sintética, proponiendo la Ética del Horizonte y el Cero Volitivo como salvaguardas existenciales necesarias para recuperar la finitud, la verdad y la agencia humanas. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used in network operations (NetOps) and artificial intelligence for IT operations (AIOps) for tasks ranging from telemetry retrieval and incident diagnosis to configuration planning and bounded remediation. As these systems acquire greater access to operational tools, the central question is no longer only what an LLM can do, but whether operational assurance increases commensurately with the authority granted to it. This survey examines that question through a structured, evidence-stratified review of agentic NetOps and AIOps. We organise the field around autonomy, tool scope, evidence traces, assurance controls, evaluation, security, and governance, and introduce an operational assurance contract that links each autonomy level to permitted tools, required evidence, independent gates, execution budgets, rollout and rollback duties, and audit requirements. The synthesis reveals a capability--assurance gap: evidence is comparatively strong for read-oriented assistance and tool-grounded diagnosis, but becomes substantially less complete as systems approach configuration change, bounded execution, and closed-loop operation. We therefore argue that evaluation should move beyond static question answering and model accuracy towards workflow-level assessment of evidence quality, tool use, policy and invariant compliance, staged execution, recovery, calibration, cost, and human intervention. We also examine prompt-borne attacks, poisoned or stale operational evidence, excessive agency, privilege boundaries, and weak auditability. Taken together, the survey frames agentic NetOps and AIOps as constrained operational control, in which useful autonomy depends on independently enforced assurance rather than model capability alone.

The auditability of large language model-based systems requires verifiable evidence without exposing the sensitive content of interactions. This article proposes a hash-chained audit-ledger framework to transform public LLM conversations into canonical off-chain units, generate cryptographic commitments using SHA-256 and HMAC-SHA-256, build a lightweight ledger with Merkle roots, and verify integrity against induced tampering. The study integrates three heterogeneous sources, LMSYS-Chat-1M, WildChat, and Chatbot Arena, and produces 3,971,887 auditable units. In the full-corpus HMAC-SHA-256 experiment, the 11,899.55 MiB normalized repository was represented by 1,473.44 MiB of hash-only audit records, 2.03 MiB of ledger block headers, and 380.52 MiB for the operational ledger plus membership structures required for record-level verification. Five induced tampering categories, Merkle and decision-hash integrity, hash-chain linkage integrity, block ordering integrity, membership completeness, and dataset-membership consistency, were detected without false acceptance; a separate clean-ledger baseline validated the untampered ledger with zero error signals. Load experiments showed near-linear growth of mean total pipeline time with respect to the number of audit records. Operational ledger-stage throughput increased across the intermediate workloads but declined at the largest evaluated load, while full record-set verification throughput remained comparatively stable up to 250,000 interactions before decreasing in the 500,000-interaction scenario. This contribution demonstrates that the traceability of decisions generated by LLM can be formulated as a measurable, private, and cryptographically verifiable experimental chain. The framework provides a documented numerical-audit basis for independent consistency assessment, regulatory compliance, and forensic analysis when ledger states are evaluated against preserved artifacts, trusted checkpoints, or externally anchored commitments.

Short-video platforms are increasingly embedded in nurses’ daily rest and emotional regulation, but problematic short-video use may be associated with impaired recovery and occupational functioning. Evidence on heterogeneous patterns of problematic short-video use among clinical nurses and their relationship with presenteeism remains limited. To identify latent profiles of problematic short-video use among nurses in tertiary Grade A hospitals and examine whether presenteeism, work interference with personal life, perceived organizational support, and relevant sociodemographic and occupational characteristics were associated with latent profile membership. A cross-sectional study was conducted from October to December 2025. A total of 700 clinical nurses from three tertiary Grade A hospitals in Wuhan were recruited using convenience sampling. After excluding 20 invalid questionnaires, 680 valid responses were included. Data were collected using a general information questionnaire, the Problematic Short-Video Use Scale-9 (PSVUS-9), the Perceived Organizational Support Scale, the Stanford Presenteeism Scale, and the five-item Work interference with personal life (WIPL) subscale of the Work/Nonwork Interference and Enhancement Scale. SPSS 27.0 was used for descriptive statistics and univariate analysis, Mplus 8.3 was used for latent profile analysis, and R software was used for multivariable multinomial logistic regression analysis. The total score for problematic short-video use among nurses in tertiary Grade A hospitals was 21.23 ± 8.80, and 38.4% of nurses were at risk of problematic use. Latent profile analysis identified three classes: the low-symptom use group, consisting of 383 nurses (56.3%); the escape-withdrawal prominent group, consisting of 226 nurses (33.2%); and the high-symptom comprehensive risk group, consisting of 71 nurses (10.5%). Significant differences were found among the three latent classes in gender, department, perceived organizational support, work interference with personal life, and presenteeism ( P < 0.05). Multinomial logistic regression showed that, after controlling for gender, department, perceived organizational support, and work interference with personal life, presenteeism was significantly associated with membership in both the escape-withdrawal prominent group (OR = 1.392, 95%CI: 1.115–1.738, P = 0.003) and the high-symptom comprehensive risk group (OR = 2.365, 95%CI: 1.641–3.409, P < 0.001). Problematic short-video use among nurses in tertiary Grade A hospitals showed obvious heterogeneity. Presenteeism was a stable factor associated with different risk classes of problematic short-video use, suggesting that high-symptom status may be closely related to impaired on-the-job functioning and insufficient recovery among nurses. Nursing managers may conduct stratified identification based on latent class characteristics and incorporate presenteeism, departmental context, and recovery resources into occupational health management for nurses.

Healthcare systems worldwide are increasingly pressured to deliver higher-quality care while minimizing delays, inefficiencies, and costs. Lean Healthcare, a process improvement methodology derived from Lean manufacturing, offers a structured framework for waste reduction, reducing patient wait times, and enhancing clinical outcomes. This paper investigates the application of core Lean principles, such as value stream mapping, standardized workflows, and continuous improvement (Kaizen), in various healthcare settings like emergency departments, outpatient clinics, and surgical care units. Drawing from recent empirical studies and real-world implementations, the research highlighted how Lean interventions have led to measurable reductions in patient wait times (ranging from 20% to 50%), improved patient flow, and better alignment of care delivery with demand. Additionally, the integration of Lean with Digital Twin, Artificial intelligence, Machine Learning as well as interdisciplinary collaboration has shown to improve care coordination, reduce medical errors, and also enhance patient satisfaction. Despite these benefits, challenges such as resistance to change, siloed processes, and limited data infrastructure still persist. The paper concludes with recommendations for sustainable Lean adoption through leadership engagement, staff training, and robust performance monitoring. Ultimately, this study underscores Lean Healthcare’s potential as a strategic tool for enhancing both operational efficiency and patient-centered outcomes in an increasingly value-driven healthcare environment.

documents.abstract: Abstract The concept of human dignity has acquired renewed philosophical significance in the light of rapid developments in biotechnology, genetic engineering, artificial intelligence, reproductive medicine and end-of-life care. While such scientific innovations offer unprecedented benefits, they can provoke reductive interpretations of the human person, encouraging the view that human beings are primarily biological organisms or technological objects. This article examined Leon Kass's conception of human dignity as an integrated philosophical framework for engaging these contemporary bioethical challenges. Drawing upon philosophical analysis and critical evaluation, the study argued that Kass's conception of human dignity is grounded on the intrinsic nature of the human person and not on autonomy, utility or social recognition. Furthermore, Kass's bioethical vision incorporated philosophical anthropology, scientific reflection and moral reasoning as a way of defending the uniqueness of human life against technological reductionism. The article contended that Kass's concept offered an important corrective to the dominant bioethical theories which privilege the individual while neglecting the ontological and moral significance of human nature. Although some aspects of Kass's conservatism were open to philosophical criticism, the integrated approach he offers, proved to be a compelling framework for understanding human dignity in an age increasingly dominated by biomedical innovation and artificial intelligence. The study concluded that Kass's vision continues to make an important contribution to contemporary debates concerning personhood, medical ethics and the moral limits of biotechnology. Keywords: Human dignity; Leon Kass; Bioethics; Philosophical anthropology; Biotechnology; Human nature; Medical ethics.

As climate change intensifies environmental and socio-economic vulnerabilities across Africa, there is a growing need for innovative, scalable solutions to support climate resilience. This study critically examines the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in enhancing climate adaptation and mitigation efforts on the continent. Employing a qualitative, multi-source research methodology, the paper synthesizes academic literature, institutional frameworks, and applied case studies to assess the integration of AI into environmental monitoring and resource management systems. Particular emphasis is placed on the use of machine learning and remote sensing technologies to support real-time data analysis, land-use classification, water resource management, and early warning systems. The Enhancing National Climate Services (ENACTS) program is analyzed as a leading case, demonstrating how the fusion of satellite and groundbased data can significantly improve climate services in sectors such as agriculture and public health. The paper also identifies critical challenges—including data scarcity, inadequate infrastructure, limited technical capacity, and ethical risks such as data privacy and algorithmic bias—that hinder the effective deployment of AI. In response, the study offers strategic policy recommendations to strengthen climate data infrastructure, promote cross-sector collaboration, and build human capital in AI and climate science. The findings underscore the importance of African-led innovation, ethical governance, and context-specific solutions in ensuring that AI contributes meaningfully and equitably to sustainable development and climate resilience.

ABSTRACT Background Ambiguities in software requirement documents, such as software requirement specifications (SRS) and user stories, pose significant challenges to the success of software development projects. These ambiguities often result in misinterpretations, inconsistent system designs, and increased costs and delays. Despite advancements in requirements engineering and natural language processing, existing methods frequently address only limited types of ambiguities or fail to integrate detection and resolution processes effectively. Aims This research introduces a framework that leverages fine‐tuned large language models (LLMs) to systematically detect and resolve ambiguities in software requirements. The framework targets seven key categories of ambiguities: semantic, syntactic, functional, operational, scope, temporal, and quality. Materials and Methods The framework uses fine‐tuned LLaMA 3 and LLaMA 3.1 models with parameter‐efficient LoRA adapters. A diverse dataset of annotated SRS documents and user stories was developed to evaluate the framework. Ambiguity classification was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 scores, while ambiguity resolution was assessed using BLEU, ROUGE, and BERTScore metrics, complemented by manual evaluation. Results The fine‐tuned models demonstrated substantial improvements in ambiguity classification and generated clear, unambiguous alternatives for ambiguous requirements. The evaluation results demonstrated the effectiveness of the proposed approach in identifying and resolving ambiguities across the targeted categories. Discussion The findings demonstrate that fine‐tuned LLMs can support comprehensive ambiguity detection and resolution across multiple software requirement formats. The framework improves the clarity and usability of requirements and can support more effective communication among software development stakeholders. Conclusion The proposed framework provides a practical solution for improving the quality of requirements documentation and addressing ambiguities across diverse formats. It can help minimize errors and enhance stakeholder communication in both agile and traditional development environments. Future research will focus on extending the framework's scalability and adaptability to diverse contexts and domain‐specific requirements.

This conceptual article develops the political implications of Jean-Pol Martin’s New Human Rights (NMR). Its central question is: if preserving human life, meeting fundamental needs and maintaining shared life-supporting conditions are accepted as binding political aims, what responsibilities follow when these conditions are systematically threatened? The framework draws on six equally important fundamental needs: thinking, health, security, social inclusion, self-realisation and participation, and meaning. It distinguishes an anthropological account of human life, an explicit normative commitment to protecting that life, and the assessment of particular political measures. The article’s specific contribution is to use the NMR both as reasons for decisive protection and as constraints on the power exercised in its name. It proposes a six-step assessment procedure addressing evidence of threats, responsibility, feasible alternatives, authority and proportionality, effects on all six needs, and implementation with ongoing review. The consequences of inaction are included alongside those of intervention. Prevention, reliability and sustainability provide the temporal orientation. Within the growing Zenodo corpus on Jean-Pol Martin’s semantic field, the article connects the anthropological and normative foundations of NMR/LdL with political protection and enforcement responsibility. It extends the preceding argument for worldwide orientation by examining how that orientation can guide effective, accountable and revisable action. Hypothetical examples illustrate civic protection, targeted restrictions on violent networks and the preservation of ecological conditions. The article presents a normative reconstruction and a proposed assessment framework; it does not claim empirical validation or establish liability in particular cases. Jean-Pol Martin supplied the theoretical framework and direction of the argument. ChatGPT assisted with conceptual reconstruction, drafting and document production. The human author retains responsibility for review and publication.

A safety instrumented system (SIS) is an automated system designed to detect and mitigate potential risk of hazardous conditions in industrial processes by taking actions to prevent or mitigate incidents. It is essential because it helps protect people, equipment, and the environment by reducing the risk of accidents in hazardous operations, such as in chemical plants, oil refineries, or power stations. While the primary objective of SIS design is safety, economic considerations, particularly lifecycle cost, play a pivotal role in decision-making during the design phase. Although research efforts exist to incorporate lifecycle cost with safety, the literature is fragmented and lacks a comprehensive lifecycle cost framework. Therefore, a systematic literature review is conducted to uncover safety instrumented systems’ lifecycle cost elements and the decision variables that impact them. The review results lead to a comprehensive and structured cost calculation framework to assess SIS designed to protect a process unit economically. Finally, this study provides perspectives on potential research directions relevant to SIS lifecycle cost, including the impact of systematic failures, cybersecurity integration, the relative weighting of different cost elements, inclusion of risk costs, and various SIS application types.

Abstract Developing constitutive models that capture how materials deform under load traditionally requires years of specialized expertise in continuum mechanics, machine learning, and scientific programming. Large language models (LLMs) have recently been shown to lower this barrier by generating constitutive models on demand, but existing single-agent pipelines lack systematic checks that the resulting models respect fundamental physical laws. To close this gap, we introduce the first multi-agent LLM-driven approach for constitutive model generation: a Creator agent proposes a model tailored to the data, while an Inspector agent critically audits each proposal against nine physical constraints and returns it for refinement whenever a violation is detected. We demonstrate this concept with constitutive artificial neural networks (CANNs) and benchmark it on brain tissue and rubber as isotropic materials, and on porcine skin tissue as a transversely isotropic material with a preferred fiber direction, using two different LLM backbones (Claude Opus 4.7 and Kimi K2.5). Whether a generated model satisfies the physical constraints is assessed numerically, by probing each constraint across a broad sample of deformation states, rotations, and perturbation directions. Adding the Inspector raises the share of exported models that pass all these checks from 90% to 95% for Opus and from 47% to 60% for Kimi. In addition, the generated models are on par with or even surpass expert-designed models in accuracy, extrapolate reliably beyond the training data, and generalize remarkably well to unseen loading paths. Separating generation from inspection thus turns LLM-driven constitutive modeling into a substantially more trustworthy process. The paradigm is deliberately technique-agnostic and scales automatically with advances in LLM capability, opening a promising path toward automated, physics-aware model discovery.

In the field of Acoustic Emission analysis, the use of artificial intelligence is becoming increasingly important. Especially for localizing Acoustic Emission events via pattern recognition of time signals, Neural Networks hold great potential. As part of this research, this potential was tested by examining the locatability of Acoustic Emission sources on a reinforced concrete beam as a result of a four-point bending test. Specifically, the experiment involved a loading that increased until fracture of the specimen, while Acoustic Emissions were measured and recorded over 16 Acoustic Emission sensors. A total of 10,343 Acoustic Emission events were captured, of which 4,102 events could be localized three-dimensionally by triangulation. The remaining 6,241 events could not be assigned locations due to either insufficient determinability of the arrival times or too large measurement deviations. In this work, the combination of neural methods from supervised and unsupervised learning was explored. The acquired events were first divided into localized and non-localized signals. The localized events were subsequently grouped into 5, 10, 15, and 20 clusters using the K-means algorithm (unsupervised learning). Furthermore, four convolutional neural networks were trained by using the clusters as classes and the assigned events as samples per class. This approach achieved assignability with an accuracy of 71–94% and allowed the previously non-localizable Acoustic Emission events to be classified and localized by these Convolutional Neural Networks.

The rapid spread of generative artificial intelligence has complicated the interpretation of authorship in educational writing and increased the need for transparent methods that distinguish machine-generated from human-written text without treating automated detection as conclusive evidence of misconduct. This study compares lexical and content-independent stylometric approaches to detecting AI-generated educational essays. The experiments used 44,868 English-language texts from the DAIGT V2 multi-source corpus, including 27,371 human-written and 17,497 AI-generated essays. The lexical representation used TF-IDF unigrams and bigrams with a Linear Support Vector Machine, while the content-independent representation consisted of fourteen structural and stylometric features classified with Logistic Regression. Human and AI texts were additionally compared using the Mann–Whitney U test and effect-size estimates. The TF-IDF model achieved 99.69% accuracy, 99.60% F1-score and 99.98% ROC-AUC on a stratified held-out test set. The stylometry-only model achieved 87.90 ± 0.40% accuracy, 84.34 ± 0.48% F1-score and 95.08 ± 0.17% ROC-AUC under five-fold stratified cross-validation. Average word length showed the strongest selected stylometric separation, while differences were also observed in text length, lexical diversity and punctuation use. The findings show that lexical information provides highly discriminative signals in the analyzed corpus, but substantial predictive information remains even when direct vocabulary is removed. The results support the use of stylometric indicators as an interpretable supplementary signal for educational text analysis, while also emphasizing that detector outputs should not be treated as definitive proof of AI use in individual student work. Robustness checks showed 99.75% accuracy after near-duplicate filtering, 96.46% accuracy for unseen prompts, and 95.39% accuracy when Llama-70B was held out, indicating measurable distribution sensitivity. The contribution is therefore a robustness-oriented comparison of established lexical and interpretable stylometric representations rather than a new classifier.

documents.abstract: Gallstones, also known as cholelithiasis, are hardened deposits of bile (digestive fluid) formed in the gallbladder. Gallstones are a common gastrointestinal condition. They often lead to complications like cholecystitis, biliary obstruction, and pancreatitis. The diagnosis of gallstones involves blood tests, ultrasonography, and Computed Tomography (CT)/Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) have revolutionized medical diagnostics and have led to an increase in the precision and efficiency of diagnosis. In this research study, multiple supervised learning techniques were used to predict the presence of gallstones in patients. The three hyperparameter tuning techniques utilized to optimize predictive performance include: grid search algorithm, randomized search algorithm and Bayesian optimization. The randomized search algorithm performed the best among the three, with an accuracy of 83%. The AdaBoost Classification and the CatBoost Classification techniques were top performers amongst the nine learning techniques utilized in this study. The customized ensemble (stacking) model achieved an F1-score of 84% (95% CI: 71.2–91.8%) and had an AUC of 0.90 using the randomized search algorithm. Further, eight Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) techniques were utilized to interpret the classification results. Vitamin D and C-Reactive Protein (CRP) were identified as the most influential factors in predicting the condition, by XAI techniques. This highlights their significant role in predictive accuracy. The proposed model demonstrates its ability to assist healthcare professionals. It would enable efficient validation of the results obtained from other diagnostic methods.

High-speed PAM-4 SerDes and wireline interconnects used in data-center, artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), chip-to-chip, and high-speed networking applications require low-power and hardware-efficient clock and data recovery (CDR) capable of maintaining accurate timing under channel impairments, jitter, and nonlinear phase-detector characteristics. Although the Mueller–Müller phase detector (MMPD) is widely adopted for baud-rate CDR due to its simplicity and robustness, its nonlinear gain characteristic introduces residual timing errors that limit tracking accuracy and increase jitter sensitivity. This work presents a hardware-efficient AI-assisted residual MMPD for baud-rate PAM-4 CDR systems. Instead of replacing the conventional phase detector, a lightweight fully connected neural network learns only the deterministic nonlinear residual correction and generates a compensation term that is added to the classical MMPD output. The proposed residual network employs a compact 1–8–8–1 architecture with ReLU activation, containing only 97 trainable parameters and enabling efficient fixed-point RTL and ASIC implementation. The proposed detector is integrated and evaluated within a complete baud-rate PAM-4 digital CDR comprising a baud-rate sampler, PAM-4 slicer, proportional–integral loop filter, and digitally controlled oscillator, while preserving the stability and low-complexity characteristics of the conventional architecture. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed detector reduces the phase-detector RMSE from 0.2088 UI to 0.0073 UI, extends the effective linear operating range from approximately ±0.12 UI to ±0.45 UI, and achieves a 13.45% reduction in closed-loop RMS timing error compared with the classical MMPD while maintaining comparable detector noise performance. Owing to its minimal computational overhead, improved detector linearity, compatibility with existing baud-rate CDR architectures, and straightforward hardware realization, the proposed residual-learning framework provides a practical and scalable solution for AI-assisted timing recovery in next-generation high-speed PAM-4 wireline and SerDes receivers.

documents.abstract: The widespread adoption of open source software (OSS) has introduced significant security risks, with malicious code poisoning attacks increasingly targeting public package registries and open-source platforms. Existing detection approaches, including heuristic-, learning-, and LLM-based methods, suffer from language-specific designs, limited generalization, and high analysis costs, making them unsuitable for large-scale multi-language analysis. To address these challenges, we propose MalTotal, a scalable and cost-effective framework for language-agnostic malicious code detection. MalTotal leverages LLM-assisted semantic reasoning to identify sensitive APIs, perform hybrid semantic slicing, and reconstruct malicious behavior contexts while reducing analysis overhead. Our evaluations show that MalTotal outperforms 8 state-of-the-art baselines, achieving an average F1-score of 93.1

The article develops a managerial framework for the joint design of storage location assignment (slotting) and order picking in smart warehouses. Design decisions are arranged in strategic, tactical and operational layers, coupled with digital enablers and human-centric constraints, and closed into a decision cycle with a re-slotting trigger. A stylised computational case compares six configurations, from manual random storage to a goods-to-person system, by an order cycle time model, cost per order line and a weighted utility under two managerial priority profiles. Supportive technologies combined with affinity-based slotting give the lowest cost per line, whereas hybrid and substitutive automation win on throughput and ergonomic load and reach cost parity only at about five times the base volume. The preferred configuration therefore follows from managerial priorities and volume rather than from technology alone.

Algorithms can be used to measure display clutter, but their validation often relies on comparing to subjective ratings, rather than to performance and attentional decrements. It is unclear which algorithms work best in different contexts. In this study, participants searched for targets in websites and maps. Feature congestion (FC), subband entropy (SE), and edge density (ED; Rosenholtz, Li, and Nakano 2007) were calculated for each image. Results showed that only FC is positively linked to response time in websites and maps, but more so for websites and moderately in both cases. SE was negatively correlated with mean saccade length in websites. In maps, all clutter metrics were positively correlated with mean fixation duration, while FC and ED were negatively correlated to mean saccade length. The findings provide recommendations for which clutter algorithms and eye tracking metrics to use for websites and maps, while suggesting caution about some metrics.

documents.abstract: Periodontitis leads to progressive destruction of periodontal supporting tissues, and conventional anti-infective therapies often fail to simultaneously achieve infection control and tissue regeneration. Due to the increasing threat of antibiotic resistance, the development of novel bioactive molecules with both anti-infective and pro-regenerative properties has become a focus of research. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), characterized by multi-target antimicrobial mechanisms and immunomodulatory functions, have attracted considerable attention in periodontal tissue regeneration. Current evidence indicates that AMPs not only inhibit periodontal pathogens and biofilm formation, but they also regulate macrophage polarization, suppress inflammatory cytokine release, and activate signaling pathways, such as Wnt/β-catenin and MAPK/ERK. These effects promote osteogenic differentiation of periodontal ligament stem cells and bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells, while enhancing angiogenesis through VEGF induction, thereby establishing a favorable immune microenvironment for periodontal regeneration. Despite these promising findings, the in vivo stability, dosage safety, and long-term mechanisms of AMPs remain to be fully elucidated. Future studies should focus on clarifying the molecular mechanisms by which AMPs regulate the periodontal immune microenvironment and angiogenesis-osteogenesis coupled regeneration. In addition, integrating structural optimization, advanced delivery systems, and artificial intelligence-assisted peptide discovery may accelerate the development and clinical translation of novel antimicrobial peptides.

Introduction Alzheimer's disease (AD) affects an estimated 55 million people worldwide and is projected to nearly double by 2050, creating a need for scalable, non-invasive AI systems that can classify disease stage, support multimodal clinical reasoning, and interact in natural language. Most deep learning work on AD focuses on single-modality classification without natural-language interaction and typically assumes complete input data. Methods We present MEMOIR-VLM (Multimodal Encoder with Missing-modality and Open-ended Inference for Retrieval), a modular two-stage vision-language framework trained and evaluated on 2,363 ADNI subjects. The first stage is a missing-modality-aware encoder that fuses T1-weighted MRI and DTI fractional anisotropy maps with structured clinical scores via cross-attention fusion with stochastic modality dropout, allowing a single set of weights to operate on any of the seven non-empty modality subsets without imputation. After CLIP/InfoNCE contrastive pretraining, the encoder is fine-tuned for multi-task prediction of 3-way diagnosis, binary diagnosis, CDR-SB, age, and sex. The second stage extends the frozen encoder into a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline for case-based reasoning and open-ended visual question answering. Results On held-out ADNI test data, with CDR-SB excluded from the inputs to remove a cognitive-score leak, the encoder achieved 91.3% balanced accuracy for CN vs. dementia and 68.2% balanced accuracy for 3-class diagnosis (macro-F1 = 0.681); age was predicted with a 5.96-year MAE. When the diagnosis field was withheld from retrieved captions, no evaluated LLM exceeded a retrieval-only k-NN majority vote (0.673), which itself closely matched the encoder's 3-class accuracy (0.682). The RAG-VQA layer showed strong text fidelity (BERTScore = 0.894; SBERT cosine similarity = 0.811). Zero-shot external validation on OASIS-3 (1,048 subjects, no diffusion data) retained 78.7% balanced accuracy for CN vs. impaired (AUC = 0.889) using identical ADNI-trained weights with the DTI branch masked. Discussion MEMOIR-VLM combines missing-modality-aware multimodal encoding, multi-task clinical prediction, and retrieval-grounded natural-language reasoning within a single modular framework. The results support using the encoder, optionally with k-NN voting, as the diagnostic component and the RAG-VQA layer as an interpretable natural-language interface that surfaces comparable cases and readable clinical summaries. The external validation results further demonstrate the practical value of the missing-modality mechanism when an imaging modality is unavailable.

Metacognition has informed research on second and foreign language (L2) learning for three decades, while AI tools have supported such learning for nearly as long. Yet, no review has examined how the field conceptualises and measures metacognition under AI mediation. This systematic review identified 60 eligible studies published between 2016 and May 2026. Each study was coded on fourteen dimensions anchored in established taxonomies and appraised with the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Only four eligible studies fall within the pre-ChatGPT portion of the review window, from January 2016 to November 2022; 56 were published during the subsequent three and a half years. Three findings emerge. First, measurement is narrowly concentrated: 98% of the 56 post-ChatGPT studies measured self-reported metacognitive regulation, and 66% relied on self-report alone. Only one study in the full corpus measured metacognitive accuracy. Five post-ChatGPT studies combined an AI-absent comparison with process-level data, and only one of these also measured judgement accuracy. Second, 41% of post-ChatGPT studies used tools that combined two or more functional orientations within a single interface, a configuration not represented by the field’s inherited four-category taxonomy of AI applications. Third, none of the 18 contrast-based studies assigned the regulatory operation to the system in place of the learner. In every design that specified the division of labour, the learner retained that operation; three designs did not specify it. The condition most in need of testing therefore remains untested. Reported findings skew positive, but correlational and qualitative designs account for a disproportionate share of that evidence. The review concludes with a research agenda centred on calibration and process data.

documents.abstract: Introduction: In the present era, customer attraction is one of the most important factors for the success of businesses, because intense competition and the numerous options available to customers have caused companies to make more efforts to attract and retain their customers. Applying new marketing strategies, providing quality services, and creating a unique experience for customers are among the factors that play a significant role in this regard. The need to attract customers and understanding the role of attraction in business decision-making is a key issue that, despite its great importance, has received less attention in the field of service marketing. Social media has become a pervasive communication tool that creates connections and opportunities for interaction with customers. In particular, attracting new customers is a fundamental issue in the Omid Entrepreneurship Fund. The goal of this fund, according to Article 6 of its statute, is to mobilize financial resources and provide facilities to individuals, especially in rural and deprived areas, industrial clusters, and entrepreneurs. In recent years, the fund has played an effective role in supporting production and job creation by increasing capital and financing stagnant production units. For example, in 1403, the Omid Entrepreneurship Fund has included financing 730 stagnant production units on its agenda. From a positive perspective, the use of social media marketing can help the Omid Entrepreneurship Fund to communicate more widely with entrepreneurs and small business owners. By using platforms such as Instagram, LinkedIn, and Telegram, the fund can better inform about financial facilities, loan conditions, and business growth strategies. Also, direct interaction with applicants and publishing entrepreneurs’ success stories increases public trust and attracts new customers to the fund’s services. Targeted marketing on social media also allows for the identification of the needs of different groups and the provision of services tailored to them. From a negative perspective, not paying attention to social media marketing can reduce public awareness of the fund’s services and miss important opportunities to attract applicants. In today’s digital world, many small businesses and entrepreneurs rely on the online space for information; as a result, the lack of an active presence in this space prevents the fund from properly delivering its message to its target audience. In addition, competition with other financial and support institutions requires the fund to use modern marketing methods; otherwise, applicants may turn to alternatives and the effectiveness of its services may decrease. Therefore, the present study answers the key question of what is the customer attraction model using social media marketing at the Omid Entrepreneurship Fund?Methodology: The present study was based on interpretive philosophy and conducted with an inductive approach. It is also an applied-developmental research in terms of its purpose and a non-experimental (descriptive) research in terms of its data collection method. A qualitative research design was used to achieve the research objective. The participant population includes university professors and experienced managers of the Omid Entrepreneurship Fund. Sampling was conducted purposively and theoretical saturation was achieved with 18 people. Interviews and a decision matrix-based questionnaire were used to collect data. The results of the qualitative section coding were validated using the Holst method (0.712) and Cohen's kappa estimate (0.655). The validity of the questionnaire was confirmed using the formal method and the reliability of the questionnaire was also confirmed by estimating the internal correlation coefficient (0.826). The analysis and coding of the interview texts were performed using the qualitative theme analysis method in MaxQDA 20 software. In the second part, the structural-interpretive modeling method and MicMac software were used to determine the relationships between the structures and design the model.Results and Discussion: In the findings section, to facilitate data analysis, the interview transcripts were loaded into MaxQDA software and reviewed several times to extract key points. In the open coding stage, 319 codes were identified and finally, using axial coding, 13 main themes and 67 basic themes were extracted. The results of the thematic analysis identified themes related to the customer attraction model through social media marketing in the Omid Entrepreneurship Fund and presented them.Conclusion: The results of the research have shown that strategic factors, artificial intelligence, and technical factors affect media management and media security. The aforementioned factors also affect media customer friendliness and media quality, and lead to the value of content, content management system, and content production principles. Finally, by creating aesthetics and interactivity, the ultimate goal of attracting customers to the Omid Entrepreneurship Fund is achieved.

Neurodegenerative diseases (NDs) comprise a heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by complex etiologies, multifactorial pathogenic mechanisms, and remarkable clinical and molecular variability. Their increasing prevalence poses an important challenge to healthcare systems, society and the global economy. Despite decades of research, effective disease-modifying therapies remain elusive, highlighting the urgent need for reliable disease models capable of unraveling pathogenic mechanisms and supporting the development of personalized therapeutic strategies. Modeling NDs remains inherently challenging, since disease onset and progression arise from the interplay among genetic factors, environmental exposures, aging, and individual pathological conditions. Consequently, similar insults may lead to distinct molecular trajectories and clinical outcomes in different subjects. Reproducing this heterogeneity, together with the prolonged temporal evolution that characterizes NDs over decades in humans, represents a major limitation of current experimental models. Here, we provide a comprehensive overview of the modeling strategies currently available for the study of NDs, spanning conventional two-dimensional cellular systems, advanced patient-derived three-dimensional organoids, complementary in vivo animal models, and rapidly evolving in silico approaches. For each model category, we discuss its historical development, current applications, future perspectives, and, critically, principal strengths and limitations in reproducing disease biology and supporting translational research. We emphasize that the growing synergy between in vitro, in vivo, and in silico methodologies, empowered by multimodal data integration and artificial intelligence, is expected to accelerate biomarker discovery, improve disease modeling, reduce experimental burden, and ultimately foster the development of personalized disease-modifying therapies for NDs.

Background Congenital uterine anomalies are clinically relevant in reproductive medicine, particularly among women with infertility, recurrent pregnancy loss, adverse obstetric outcomes, or obstructive symptoms. Hysteroscopy has transformed the management of correctable intracavitary anomalies by enabling conservative, image-guided reconstruction of the uterine cavity while avoiding the morbidity of historical abdominal metroplasty. Scope This narrative review critically examines contemporary hysteroscopic management of septate uterus, dysmorphic uterus, bicorporeal septate uterus and rare obstructive malformations, such as Robert's uterus. We discuss the implications of the ESHRE/ESGE, CUME, and ASRM classification systems; the role of three-dimensional transvaginal ultrasound and magnetic resonance imaging in preoperative mapping; and the technical principles that guide metroplasty, cavity remodeling, ultrasound-guided hysteroscopy, office-based metroplasty, and staged approaches in complex anatomy. Discussion Bipolar saline-based platforms, miniaturized resectoscopes, bipolar needle electrodes, cold scissors, and selected tissue removal systems have expanded the therapeutic spectrum and improved safety. The evidence supporting surgery remains heterogeneous: the TRUST randomized trial challenged routine septum resection in unselected women, whereas data for T-shaped and other dysmorphic uteri remain largely observational. Emerging technologies, including laser platforms, artificial intelligence-assisted hysteroscopy, and robotic concepts, are promising, but currently lack prospective validation. Conclusion Optimal management should therefore be individualized, anatomy-driven, and grounded in shared decision-making, with careful preservation of endometrium and myometrium. Standardized reporting, multicenter registries, and prospective comparative studies are needed to define which patients benefit most from hysteroscopic correction.

This study investigates design collaborations in interdisciplinary work settings, where actors from product design, product development, product management, marketing, production, purchasing, and quality units participate in product design processes, with the aim of contributing to both its theoretical understanding and effective management. By bridging research on design collaboration with motivational theory, the study argues that motivation constitutes a critical yet underexplored dimension of interdisciplinary design collaborations. Adopting an interpretivist approach, the research explores the experiences of twenty-five experts from diverse disciplines through semi-structured interviews. The findings identify three sets of motivational factors: (1) design-specific intrinsic motivational factors of collaboration—belief in the project, continuous progress, and continuous learning; (2) relational factors as distinct motivational drivers through constructive conflict and a sense of “we”; and (3) extrinsic factors that condition rather than generate motivation by shaping the context of collaboration. This article proposes a layered model in which intrinsic, relational, and extrinsic factors interact dynamically to sustain collaborative engagement.

Natural hazards can disrupt transport infrastructure through spatially heterogeneous flooding, seismic shaking, terrain conditions, and observed ground motion, while local exposure alone does not determine system-wide consequences. This study develops a reproducible multi-hazard Graph Artificial Intelligence framework for infrastructure resilience screening on the Romanian strategic road network. A frozen attributed line graph combines network topology with European land-cover, terrain, seismic, flood, and ground-motion evidence, and an independent disruption simulator provides continuous resilience-loss targets. GCN, GraphSAGE, and GAT were trained under a leakage-controlled three-seed protocol. On the blind 194-scenario PRIMARY TEST, ensemble RMSE/R2 were 0.013343/0.997104 for GCN, 0.013978/0.996822 for GraphSAGE, and 0.015830/0.995924 for GAT. A fresh GCN branch achieved RMSE/R2 = 0.018230/0.995852 on 111 component-disjoint cases and 0.010468/0.991654 on 256 severity-specific held-out cases. On 208 predefined external anchors held out from Graph-AI fitting and selection, GAT attained the lowest ensemble RMSE (0.021620; R2 = 0.975065), while seismic-only transfer remained weak (n = 10; R2 = 0.251–0.386). A frozen six-family GCN ablation (18 checkpoints; 194 matched test scenarios) found RMSE = 0.026175 after seismic feature omission versus 0.013343 for the full-input GCN; this is simulator-specific sensitivity, not causal hazard attribution. The results support accurate emulation of the frozen simulator and transfer-aware screening, not structural safety certification. The model outputs are simulator-based rather than observed disruption outcomes; neither an end-to-end simulator-to-GNN speedup nor calibrated prediction intervals are established by the present evaluation.

Tabular machine learning models are widely used in high-stakes domains such as finance, healthcare, and network intrusion detection, where their reliability depends heavily on accurate training labels. However, malicious or accidental label flipping can corrupt training data and degrade downstream model performance. Recent attacks further target decision-boundary or vulnerable local regions rather than flipping labels randomly. This paper presents a BYOL-based multi-view KNN sanitization approach for identifying suspicious label-flipped samples in tabular data. The method learns label-independent representations and examines KNN label-disagreement patterns across original and perturbed SSL embedding views. We evaluate the method on six cross-domain tabular benchmarks under both large-scale and small-scale label-flipping attacks, and compare it with existing sanitization baselines and a SCARF-based representation baseline. The results show that multi-view neighborhood probing improves suspicious-label detection and provides a practical F1-oriented trade-off, while downstream recovery remains attack- and target-model-dependent. These findings provide actionable insights for improving the robustness and label integrity of tabular machine learning systems against label-flipping attacks.

This chapter explores the role of multimedia and interactive technologies in enhancing creativity and conceptual understanding in STEAM education. It emphasizes cognitive, constructivist, and sociocultural learning theories, discussing how digital systems, AI, and interactive tools facilitate deep learning and creativity. Key topics include the use of instructional videos, simulations, and design principles fostering cognitive engagement, as well as immersive technologies like AR, VR, and XR that enhance experiential learning. Additionally, it addresses AI's contributions to adaptive learning, smart feedback, and innovative methods for assessing creativity and concept comprehension, while also considering ethical issues, inclusive design, and future research directions.

Abstract Murray Stein’s Jung’s Map of the Soul—Deeper Explorations renews his introduction to Analytical Psychology through Jung’s imaginative writings, correspondence, and later interpreters. Its account of individuation illuminates psychological growth, symbolic experience, and clinical responsibility. This essay examines Stein’s explanations of evolution and Code Biology: development before birth, the citation linking neural and archetypal codes, and a non-biological code rooted in spirit. It also considers his boundary between human and artificial intelligence and proposes a relational account of the Self as the developing organization of bodily and psychological processes. The assessment distinguishes codes from their products, developmental possibilities from fixed programs, and psychological significance from proof about the nature of reality. These distinctions clarify the book’s claims and contribution. The essay invites investigation of archetypal organization and possible continuities between biological and technological intelligence, while preserving the openness to symbols that gives Stein’s account much of its value.

Abstract: Pediatric sepsis involves dynamic, developmentally conditioned immune dysfunction that a single cytokine concentration or one-time severity label cannot represent. This structured narrative Review examines how nano-enabled microfluidic systems could support blood-sparing, serial assessment of functional immune states in the pediatric intensive care unit (PICU). We separate soluble-protein concentration, cell phenotype, ex vivo stimulation response, cellular effector function, immunometabolic function, and physiology, linking each measurement class to its evidence level and permitted inference. Direct pediatric studies support the biological relevance of longitudinal antigen-presentation, inducible cytokine, lymphocyte, and metabolic readouts, but cohorts remain few, small, and heterogeneous; secondary-infection findings are conflicting. Recent pediatric studies of serial soluble biomarkers and temperature trajectories expand monitoring evidence but do not validate functional immune trajectories. Engineering studies demonstrate nanoscale capture, amplification, transduction, and low-volume processing, including portable multicytokine sensing, yet these Level 4 results do not constitute pediatric clinical validity. We propose a staged sample-to-answer architecture. It distinguishes patient draw from device input, controls stimulation and preanalytics, retains developmental context, and progresses from analytical validation through pediatric feasibility and clinical validity to prospective prediction and decision utility. Artificial intelligence is restricted to age adjustment, longitudinal modeling, multimodal fusion, uncertainty display, and clinician- or nurse-facing visualization. Within the verified accessible corpus through 16 September 2026, no prospectively validated pediatric longitudinal immune-function trajectory model or nano-enabled functional immune assay for immunomodulatory treatment selection was identified. The near-term objective is a verifiable measurement-and-interpretation pathway, not an autonomous treatment selector, tested in multicenter serial cohorts with transparent blood-volume accounting, independent validation, and PICU human-factors evaluation. Keywords: sepsis, pediatrics, nanomedicine, microfluidics, functional immunomonitoring, blood-sparing diagnostics

Debate about interrogational torture still returns to the ticking-bomb scenario, despite the weight of evidence that it neither works nor withstands moral scrutiny. The post-9/11 record, from Abu Ghraib to the CIA black sites, already marked a decisive shift toward psychological forms of coercion. The technologies now emerging make a different kind of coercion possible. This paper argues that defence-funded brain-computer interfaces, of which Synchron's Stentrode is the clearest current example, combined with large language models and fusion databases, could support what I call nano-totalitarianism: the convergence of pervasive personal data, neurodata, adaptive AI, and technologically mediated coercion in ways that could penetrate or continuously condition the inner sphere of the person. Operationalised, this is a self-sustaining regime in which a detainee is held in continuous psychological distress through fabricated scenarios, interference with memory, and synthetic social contact. Such a system would turn neuroplasticity into an instrument, laying down durable neural pathways of fear, while automated monitoring assesses compliance in real time. Its lineage runs from MKULTRA's psychochemical experiments to the extraction logic of surveillance capitalism, and its endpoint is a panopticon inside the skull. The essay proceeds anticipatorily, distinguishing throughout between demonstrated current capability, plausible convergence of existing components, and speculative future possibility.

Abstract: This study examines the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the thesis supervision process for students in the Islamic Communication and Broadcasting Study Program at Sulthan Thaha Saifuddin State Islamic University (UIN) Jambi. Employing a qualitative approach, the study involved in-depth interviews with 10 students who were actively completing their undergraduate theses during the 2025/2026 academic year and five thesis supervisors. The findings indicate that the integration of AI provides various benefits, including increased efficiency, more personalized guidance, and improved accessibility to academic references. Students reported that AI accelerated the thesis revision process by providing real-time feedback and recommendations for relevant literature. Meanwhile, lecturers experienced a reduced administrative workload through the automation of routine tasks, allowing them to focus more on providing guidance on conceptual and methodological aspects. The recommendations emphasize the importance of institutional policies to enhance technology training and develop digital infrastructure for academic staff and students. Thus, AI can be effectively integrated to support the thesis supervision process and help students achieve their academic potential more optimally. The main limitation of this study lies in its limited sample size, which prevents the findings from being statistically generalized. In addition, the findings reflect a specific phase of generative AI adoption that may change in response to the rapid evolution of the technology.Abstrak: Penelitian ini mengkaji penggunaan Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) dalam proses pembimbingan skripsi bagi mahasiswa Program Studi Komunikasi dan Penyiaran Islam di Universitas Islam Negeri (UIN) Sulthan Thaha Saifuddin Jambi. Dengan menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif, penelitian ini melibatkan wawancara mendalam terhadap 10 mahasiswa yang sedang aktif menyelesaikan tugas akhir pada tahun akademik 2025/2026 serta lima dosen pembimbing. Temuan penelitian menunjukkan bahwa integrasi AI memberikan berbagai manfaat, seperti peningkatan efisiensi, bimbingan yang lebih personal, dan aksesibilitas yang lebih baik terhadap referensi akademik. Mahasiswa melaporkan bahwa AI mempercepat proses revisi skripsi dengan memberikan umpan balik secara real-time dan rekomendasi literatur yang relevan. Sementara itu, dosen merasakan berkurangnya beban kerja administratif berkat otomatisasi tugas-tugas rutin, sehingga mereka dapat lebih fokus pada pemberian arahan terkait aspek konseptual dan metodologis. Rekomendasi yang diajukan menekankan pentingnya kebijakan institusional untuk meningkatkan pelatihan teknologi serta mengembangkan infrastruktur digital bagi staf akademik dan mahasiswa. Dengan demikian, AI dapat diintegrasikan secara efektif untuk mendukung proses pembimbingan skripsi dan membantu mahasiswa mencapai potensi akademik mereka secara optimal. Keterbatasan utama studi ini terletak pada cakupan sampel yang terbatas, sehingga temuan ini tidak dapat digeneralisasi secara statistik Selain itu, temuan mencerminkan fase tertentu adopsi AI generatif yang berpotensi berubah seiring laju evolusi teknologi.

documents.abstract: Purpose This study examines how consumers' ethical perceptions and relationship quality influence chatbot adoption in social commerce, using an extended Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2) model. The study specifically emphasizes the role of ethical considerations and relationship dynamics in shaping users' continuous intention to use chatbots. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected through an online survey targeting social commerce customers in the United States and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings The results reveal that performance expectancy, effort expectancy, hedonic motivation, habit and ethical perception significantly influence relationship quality. Relationship quality and consumers' ethical perception significantly influence continuous intention to use chatbots. Facilitating conditions showed a negative impact on relationship quality, while social influence demonstrated no significant effect. Research limitations/implications The study's focus on US customers may limit its generalizability to other cultural contexts and geographical regions. Practical implications Social commerce businesses can utilize these insights to enhance chatbot implementation, foster customer engagement and address ethical concerns, ultimately improving continuous usage intention. The findings have broader social implications for understanding the acceptance of technology and ethical practices in contemporary society. Originality/value This study extends the consumers' ethical theory model by incorporating relationship quality and technology usage as key factors in understanding chatbot adoption in social commerce, addressing a gap in the existing literature regarding the integration of artificial intelligence chatbots and social commerce platforms.

documents.abstract: Background: Difficult airway management requires appropriate assessment, planning, technical skills, teamwork, and effective use of cognitive aids. Human factors may influence decision-making during challenging airway situations. This study explored the experiences of airway practitioners and identified facilitators and barriers in routine airway instrumentation using the SEIPS framework. Methods: A qualitative study using thematic analysis based on Braun and Clarke’s approach was conducted at a tertiary care center in Kottayam, Kerala. Fifteen anaesthesiologists or emergency physicians with at least five years of airway-management experience were purposively selected. Data were collected through in-depth face-to-face interviews conducted between October 2024 and October 2025. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using an inductive approach, with themes and subthemes developed and reviewed by the investigators. Results: Three initial codes, five major themes, and 15 subthemes emerged from the interviews. The major themes were clinical and problem-solving skills, training and teamwork, overcoming challenges, the role of tools in clinical decision-making, and sources of error in clinical decisions. Participants emphasized appropriate airway assessment, timely decision-making, teamwork, supervision, access to advanced airway devices, updated knowledge, and effective communication. Uncertainty from previous experiences, overconfidence, cognitive overload, poor communication, and system-related constraints were identified as barriers. Conclusion: Standardization, updated knowledge, teamwork, leadership, effective communication, and appropriate cognitive aids may help address challenges in airway management and bridge gaps between policy and clinical practice.

Abstract India’s National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 articulates an ambitious vision for the comprehensive reform of higher education, foregrounding technology integration, multidisciplinary learning, and learner-centred pedagogy as central pillars. Concurrently, the global proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) across educational domains has prompted serious scholarly and policy-level engagement with its transformative potential and inherent risks. This paper presents a critical analysis of the intersection between NEP 2020 and AI-driven transformation in three core dimensions of higher education: teaching, learning, and assessment. Drawing upon verified policy documents, systematic reviews, and empirical studies published by reputable international bodies and journals between 2016 and 2025, the paper examines how NEP 2020’s policy architecture creates both affordances and constraints for AI adoption. The analysis reveals that while the policy’s emphasis on digital infrastructure, personalised learning, and continuous assessment aligns substantively with global AI-in-education trajectories, significant challenges persist regarding equitable access, faculty preparedness, ethical governance, and assessment integrity. The paper argues that realising NEP 2020’s AI-enabled vision demands a critical, context-sensitive implementation strategy that moves beyond techno-optimism toward principled, evidence-informed integration.

DESCRIPTION OBSERVE Protocol v1.0 — Version 7 defines a longitudinal research infrastructure for transforming institutional communications, responses, actions, permissions, public-record pathways, and digitally observable events into structured, verifiable, provenance-aware research evidence. Version 7 extends the methodological foundations established in Versions 1–6 by explicitly treating institutional communication as a research event that can be recorded, verified, preserved, compared, and connected to subsequent open research outputs. The framework does not treat institutional communication as a conclusion in itself. Acknowledgement, substantive review, permission, endorsement, public-record inclusion, policy adoption, and observable institutional change are maintained as distinct evidence categories. This distinction is essential for preventing overstatement while preserving the research value of institutional interactions. Version 7 incorporates a new phase of the longitudinal observation record involving institutional communication concerning AI accountability, software and agentic AI identity and authorization, Citizen Auditing, and research provenance. It documents how external research contributions can enter institutional communication channels, how acknowledgement and public-record pathways can be preserved as research events, and how such interactions may subsequently generate new open research outputs. A central example is the documented research interaction with the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) / National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence (NCCoE) concerning software and agentic AI identity and authorization. The corresponding research record connects institutional AI-accountability work with the OBSERVE methodology, longitudinal institutional observation, research provenance, and open research. Version 7 also records a separate administrative communication concerning a Public-Interest Research Contribution: Citizen Auditing and AI Accountability. The communication established an administrative acknowledgement and a pathway for potential public sharing in future meeting minutes. The researcher's confirmation of permission is preserved as a provenance event. The framework does not interpret this acknowledgement or permission as substantive institutional review, endorsement, policy adoption, or validation of the underlying research. The same provenance principle is extended to communications with academic units concerning quotation, citation, attribution, and permission to reuse research material. Such communications are treated as research-provenance events because they document how research material moves between researchers, institutions, academic audiences, and subsequent publications. The methodological cycle remains: OBSERVE → RECORD → VERIFY → PRESERVE → COMPARE → RESPOND → LEARN Version 7 therefore expands the original observation model into the following research-evidence pathway: Institutional Communication → Observation → Evidence → Research Provenance → Open Research Output → Longitudinal Analysis → Learning The framework establishes explicit boundaries between: acknowledgement and substantive review; permission and endorsement; public-record pathways and confirmed publication; temporal sequence and causal evidence; institutional communication and institutional adoption; research dissemination and institutional validation. This bounded-inference approach enables institutional interactions to be studied without converting administrative communication into unsupported conclusions. Version 7 further connects OBSERVE with emerging AI Accountability Literacy, particularly the methodological questions of how AI actions can be identified, authenticated, authorized, observed, recorded, verified, and preserved as research evidence. The framework is designed for research involving digital platforms, public and private institutions, regulatory environments, AI systems, agentic AI, citizen auditing, institutional observation, research provenance, open science, and longitudinal accountability research. Its central methodological proposition is: When institutional accountability increasingly depends upon traceable evidence, the provenance, verification, preservation, and longitudinal comparability of institutional observation become part of the research infrastructure through which accountability can be studied. OBSERVE Protocol v1.0 — Version 7 is therefore not a legal framework, regulatory assessment, judicial determination, or institutional evaluation. It is a research and evidence infrastructure designed to make institutional observation reproducible, auditable, provenance-aware, and suitable for longitudinal research. Version 7 treats the research record as cumulative. Earlier observations are not overwritten by later developments. New institutional communications, responses, permissions, public records, publications, technical changes, non-responses, and other observable events are added as subsequent research events. The record remains open to verification, comparison, and learning. The framework does not interpret this acknowledgement or permission as substantive institutional review, endorsement, policy adoption, or validation of the underlying research. The same provenance principle is extended to communications with academic units concerning quotation, citation, attribution, and permission to reuse research material. Such communications are treated as research-provenance events because they document how research material moves between researchers, institutions, academic audiences, and subsequent publications. The methodological cycle remains: OBSERVE → RECORD → VERIFY → PRESERVE → COMPARE → RESPOND → LEARN Version 7 therefore expands the original observation model into the following research-evidence pathway: Institutional Communication → Observation → Evidence → Research Provenance → Open Research Output → Longitudinal Analysis → Learning The framework establishes explicit boundaries between: acknowledgement and substantive review; permission and endorsement; public-record pathways and confirmed publication; temporal sequence and causal evidence; institutional communication and institutional adoption; research dissemination and institutional validation. This bounded-inference approach enables institutional interactions to be studied without converting administrative communication into unsupported conclusions. Version 7 further connects OBSERVE with emerging AI Accountability Literacy, particularly the methodological questions of how AI actions can be identified, authenticated, authorized, observed, recorded, verified, and preserved as research evidence. The framework is designed for research involving digital platforms, public and private institutions, regulatory environments, AI systems, agentic AI, citizen auditing, institutional observation, research provenance, open science, and longitudinal accountability research. Its central methodological proposition is: When institutional accountability increasingly depends upon traceable evidence, the provenance, verification, preservation, and longitudinal comparability of institutional observation become part of the research infrastructure through which accountability can be studied. OBSERVE Protocol v1.0 — Version 7 is therefore not a legal framework, regulatory assessment, judicial determination, or institutional evaluation. It is a research and evidence infrastructure designed to make institutional observation reproducible, auditable, provenance-aware, and suitable for longitudinal research. Version 7 treats the research record as cumulative. Earlier observations are not overwritten by later developments. New institutional communications, responses, permissions, public records, publications, technical changes, non-responses, and other observable events are added as subsequent research events. The record remains open to verification, comparison, and learning.
